message:
release(0.2.115): the first release that carries the orphan fix

0.2.114 had only the Client check fix. A machine that installs it gets a visible
update button and hits the orphan race the moment it is pressed, so 0.2.114 is not
the release to bootstrap a remote machine with -- this one is.

Four artifacts changed: Host (orphan fix, 660480 -> 664064), Client, Setup and the
updater itself (17ecfa1e -> fd948c7f). The updater changing matters: whether it
replaces its own bytes is the field observation, and an identical binary would have
made that unobservable.

Both pre-publish gates pass: the payload-set gate agrees name for name with
product_payload_names(), and remote60_verify_release accepts the real document with
the key compiled into the product and refuses it with one byte changed. Published in
the fixed order, then the served document was fetched back and re-verified -- byte
identical to what was signed -- and all ten public URLs were downloaded anonymously
and hashed. 0.2.111..0.2.114 artifacts unchanged; the 0.2.114 pair is backed up.

Publishing is not passing. The field test is still open, so its procedure and, more
to the point, its recovery procedure are written down first: on 2026-09-11 this
machine was left unusable twice and nothing recorded what to look at or what to undo.
